title: I Can Split My Ants Infinitely with SSS Talent—Stopped Counting After Millions and Trillions
transcript: Niuyue City, in front of First People's Hospital. " Don't go, brother. You'll die." Tears streamed down the girl's face as she sat in her wheelchair, gripping my hand tight. "Mom and Dad are already gone. Xiaoyu can't lose you too." " Relax." I placed my hand on her forehead, my gaze unwavering. "I watch twelve hours of survival shows every day. I'm not gonna die." The year is 2026. Countless rifts have torn open in the skies above Blue Star, and alien races have poured through in force. Humanity has been beaten back again and again, our living space crushed down to just thirteen cities across the Federation. Our only hope lies in that survival game space. Those who make it out alive become the Gifted— beings who can fly through the skies, burrow through the earth, split mountains and part seas. Humanity's last line of defense. The catch? That place only opens once a year, with a death rate of 99%. Three years ago, my parents were forcibly sent in and never came back. Now the Federation has dropped the entry age to eighteen. I just turned eighteen this year. " Doesn't our family have an exemption slot? Use it, brother, quick!" Xiaoyu clung to me, refusing to let go. When two members of a family have entered the survival space, that family earns a single exemption slot. Use it, and you can refuse entry forever. But I can't use it. My sister is fifteen, both legs paralyzed. In three years, it'll be her turn— and going in means certain death. " The slot's for you. Be good." I steeled myself and pried her hand off mine. " Oh, what touching sibling devotion." The screech of an engine cut through the air as a red sports car skidded to a stop like a bolt of lightning. The door opened, and out stepped a woman in a tight black dress—Liu Ruyan, my fiancée in name only. Behind her trailed a well-dressed rich boy, the two of them arm in arm. " Three years ago you showed up out of nowhere waving a marriage contract," I said, eyeing her coldly. " I knew from the start—you were only after the exemption slot." " So what? The contract's recognized by the Federation. That makes me half a member of the Wang family." Liu Ruyan tightened her grip on the man's shoulder. "You want to use the slot? Did you ask me first?" The man let out a cold laugh. Zhao Ritian—son of the deputy governor of Tianyuan City. " Kid, be smart and hand over the slot." He spoke slowly, deliberately. " Maybe I could get my father to fix your sister's legs." My whole body went rigid. Six months ago, during an alien invasion, a fallen roof beam crushed Xiaoyu's legs. The city doctors were helpless—only a Gifted could heal her. " Young Master Zhao, the slot has to go to me!" Liu Ruyan panicked. "Those crippled legs—wasn't that you who—" " Shut up! You idiot." Zhao Ritian's expression changed in an instant. " You took matters into your own hands with Wang Chufeng's parents. I haven't even settled that score with you yet—" He cut himself off abruptly. But I'd already understood. My sister's legs—he was the one who broke them. My parents' disappearance—Liu Ruyan had a hand in it. Bloodlust surged in my chest. I clenched my fists so hard they shook. knuckles white. " You," I said, spacing out each word, "wait for me in the survival world. I won't let you off." " Ha, Young Master Zhao is the son of the Deputy City Lord. How could he possibly enter the Survival Space?" Liu Ruyan sneered. "Quit dreaming, you broke loser. Hand over the slot today, or your whole family dies." " That's right. My dad's a gifted one who came out of the Space—one of humanity's top hundred fighters." Zhao Ritian dropped all pretense. "Even if you lowlifes all die out, I still can't get in." I smiled. I pointed at the phone stand by the flower bed. " I've been livestreaming this whole time. Every second, on camera—right now there are, what, a few hundred thousand people watching?" Both their faces went white in an instant, their legs buckling beneath them. Only a billion people were left on Earth. A few hundred thousand viewers now was the equivalent of tens of millions ten years ago. With the Deputy City Lord's son acting this arrogant in public, not even his father's overwhelming power could suppress this tidal wave of public rage. " Damn it! You set me up!" Zhao Ritian collapsed to the ground. I unclenched my fist and looked toward Xiaoyu. Xiaoyu, big brother can finally go in with peace of mind. As for revenge—inside the Survival Space, I'll collect it from them with my own hands. The transport array blazed with light, and the world spun. When I opened my eyes again, I was standing in a gray, hazy space. A cold, mechanical voice sounded: 【Welcome to the Survival Game World. This session: Beast Taming Survival.】 【Difficulty: Extreme. Players receive two draws: a Fated Beast card and a Beast Talent card.】 I slowly reached out and flipped over the two cards floating before me. The chance to defy fate and rewrite my destiny had finally come. 【Note: Talents can only be applied to your Fated Beast. If your Fated Beast dies, the talent becomes void, and the player suffers a severe backlash injury. If the player dies, the beast dies.】 My heart tightened. I had to draw a beast that wasn't easy to kill. Otherwise, the moment it died, I'd be completely finished. The first card flipped over, and the phantom images of all kinds of animals flickered wildly— cattle and sheep of the grasslands, giant fish of the deep sea, even the dragons and phoenixes of legend. Finally, the image locked onto— An ant. 【Fated Beast: Leafcutter Ant Quality: Common (Lowest Tier) Level: 0 Combined Combat Power: 0.01 Talent: None Description: Extraordinarily weak. A single raindrop spells total annihilation. Cuts through wooden objects relatively quickly. Rating: The lowliest of the lowly!】 I stared at the sesame-sized black speck in my palm. Eight quality tiers, and I'd drawn the worst—Common. And not just Common, but the weakest ant among the Common tier. I could crush it just by sitting down carelessly. Whatever. I flipped over the second card, the Talent card. Letters rolled by in a frenzy—A, B, C, D, E, S—and finally stopped at: SSS. My pupils contracted. 【Talent: Infinite Division Quality: S ** SS Rank** Description: As long as energy is sufficient, you can infinitely split your beast. Each copy possesses the full power of the original. The stronger the beast, the more energy it consumes. Energy Source: Energy Coins Rating: The only SSS-grade talent in this survival space!】 My breath caught. The weakest beast, but the strongest talent. Even the weakest ant, in infinite numbers, can grind out a qualitative change. The key was Energy Coins. As I pondered, the gray mist dissolved. Solid wooden walls materialized out of nowhere, along with a bed and a stone pickaxe-axe lying on the floor. A broken wooden door, drafty windows, the stench of rotting timber. Outside was pitch black, filled with the overlapping howls of unknown creatures. This was the spawn point. 【Rule 1: Survive 100 days to clear the game.】 【Rule 2: Daytime is relatively safe—gather, hunt, and open treasure chests to level up. Nighttime is extremely dangerous— stay inside your cabin.】 【Rule 3: The nights grow increasingly deadly. Keep upgrading your cabin— it's your only hope of surviving to day 100.】 【Rule 4: The first three days are the newbie protection period.】 【Rule 5: A desperate disaster strikes every seven days. On the seventh day, a horde of beast corpses will erupt.】 Food and water were entirely up to you to find. That rule alone would wipe out a huge chunk of people. 【Game start. Panel unlocked. Silently focus to toggle the panel.】 Panel. A pale blue interface appeared, with three functions: Regional Channel, Trading Market, and Building Info. I opened the Regional Channel—Niuyue City Region. Population: 20,098. A city of over ten million people, yet only twenty thousand had entered. Messages scrolled endlessly: Zhang Jiwei - Silver Leech: That's it? I'm the champion of a wilderness survival competition. Lin Guorui - Golden Otter: I pulled a Golden Otter, B-grade talent! Lin Wenshu - Mythical Flood Dragon: You're all pathetic. Watch me go out there and slaughter everything! Someone had actually pulled a Mythical rank. I was about to ask about Energy Coins when the channel suddenly flashed— 【Lin Wenshu - Mythical Flood Dragon, DEAD!】 Mythical rank, dead in just seconds? Terror seized everyone in an instant. I jerked back against the bed, curling up, and only then caught the time in the corner of the panel: 【Time until daytime: 10 minutes】 I understood now. He'd opened the cabin door and walked into the night—killed instantly. Something in the darkness could one-shot even a Mythical rank. I immediately opened the building tab. 【Small Cabin Level: 0 Durability: 2/100 (drops 1 point every half hour at night; 1 wood repairs 2 points) Upgrade Materials: 50 units of wood Rating: Severely damaged!】 Only 2 durability left. An hour at most. Wood. I had to get wood. In the channel, everyone else was catching on too: Sun Ya - ** Bronze Fathead Fish:** Anyone got wood? I'll trade silk stockings for it! ** ZhaoRiTian-DiamondSaberTooth:** I'm ZhaoRiTian, son of the Deputy City Lord. Bring me wood and you'll be richly rewarded! ZhaoRiTian. The corner of my mouth curled up. So he'd finally been driven in here by that overwhelming tide of public outrage. Good. That blood debt—I would settle it right here, with my own hands. Sunlight pierced through the cracks. Daytime had arrived. I gripped my pickaxe and pushed open the cabin door. Golden morning light bathed the forest, distant peaks wreathed in thin mist. It wasn't the post-apocalyptic wasteland I'd imagined—instead, it teemed with life. But I didn't dare let my guard down for even a second—even the legendary Flood Dragon had gone down. ** 【Pickaxe** ** Attack Power: 2** ** Durability: 30/30 (Irreparable)** ** Description: Can harvest Level 0 trees and ore.** ** Rating: It'll have to do!】** I tapped the grass lightly with the back of the axe, confirmed there was no ambush, then advanced step by step. Moments later, I came to a tree about as thick as a bowl's rim. The instant my eyes landed on it, a faint glow rose around its edges— like a file selected with a mouse. I swung the stone axe. Wood chips flew everywhere. I lost count of how many times I chopped before the tree finally crashed to the ground, turning into three pieces of wood. ** 【Obtained 3 units of wood】** I glanced at the time—it had somehow eaten up over an hour. My heart sank. A full day of hard chopping would yield six or seven pieces at most, barely enough to make it through one night. But I still had to eat and drink, and monsters would attack the cabin after dark. My axe only had 25 durability left too. Chopping like this, I was as good as dead. Stay calm. Beast taming. This game was called *Beast Taming Survival*, and the key to breaking through lay with the beasts themselves. But activating their talents required energy coins. I opened the shop. The balance in the upper left corner—0. The shop had two tabs: Player Listings and System Buyback. The buyback prices were low, but it was my only source right now. I tapped "exchange." ** 【Detected 3 units of wood, can be recycled for 3 energy copper coins. Recycle?】** Recycle. Three coins glowing with green light appeared in my palm, each the size of a one-yuan piece— a forest on the front, a blurry human figure on the back. I returned to the cabin and found that little black ant in the corner. ** 【Use Infinite Division on the Leafcutter Ant?】** Yes. In an instant— One became two, two became four. Within a single breath, the bed board was blanketed in a solid layer of black. Thirty thousand little black ants, every single one a true body. As long as one survived, my beast would never die. I stared at the three vanished copper coins, my blood surging. With enough energy, I could drown this entire world in ants. " Little blacks, move out." I left ten behind to guard the true body while the rest poured out. I split off a portion to scatter and scout, and the remainder swarmed to attack the trees. A single ant couldn't fell a tree. But tens of thousands working at once— * Rustle* Rustling, swarming like a rising tide. The base of the tree trunk quickly split into a visible notch. My stone axe wasn't idle either, chopping alongside the ants. One hour later. Four massive trees toppled one after another, and twelve logs flashed onto the ground. Recycle—twelve copper coins credited. I activated my talent again. Ten thousand, twenty thousand, thirty thousand... One hundred twenty thousand ants took shape in mere seconds. Together with the previous ones, a full one hundred fifty thousand. Truly worthy of being the only SSS-rank talent. With enough energy, even ants can raise a tsunami. I was about to swing my axe when an urgent buzzing from Little Black suddenly echoed in my mind. To the southeast, a scouting ant had spotted a creature— And on its back, it carried a treasure chest. The rules had said that treasure chests held special resources. My eyes lit up. I hefted my pickaxe and crept toward it. Fifty meters southeast of the cabin. The bushes shook violently, and a wild boar leapt out. Dozens of pounds, grunting as it rooted through the dirt in search of food. On its back sat a shoebox-sized black iron chest—not strapped on, but literally smashed into its spine. Pus dripped down from the rotting flesh, the stench overwhelming. Its eyes were cloudy and lifeless. A zombie boar. I immediately ducked back behind the tree. No matter how good the treasure was, my life mattered more. One bite from that thing, one viral infection, and I'd be finished right here. Can't rush this. With a single thought, twenty thousand Little Blacks scattered silently, locking onto the boar from every direction. The prey couldn't escape. I'd go back to chopping trees first. One hour. Crash—eleven trees fell one after another, opening a clearing in the forest as sunlight poured in. [ Beast Master chopped a Level 0 tree, obtained Wood ×3] The notification chimed nonstop. Thirty-nine logs—I recycled them all, and a small handful of energy copper coins instantly piled up in my palm. " Little Black, unlimited division." One became two, two became four. The black tide beneath my feet expanded wildly at a visible pace. For several meters in every direction, a dense black mass. Five hundred ten thousand. Staggering. I stared at this army of ants, pondering for just an instant. Chase the boar? No way to catch it. Ants are too slow, and the boar would bolt the moment it ran—unless I surrounded it completely. " Keep gnawing the trees." Four hundred thousand stayed to devour the wood, while one hundred thousand fanned out to scout in all directions— if there was one monster and one treasure chest, then there had to be a second one, and a second chest. Another hour. Forty-one trees came crashing down. " Recycle—one hundred twenty-three logs." Copper coins spilled through the gaps between my fingers. " Divide." One million six hundred thirty thousand Little Blacks gnawed in unison. The scene was like a moving black ocean. The pickaxe's durability hit zero and crumbled to dust. Two hours left until nightfall. The last time. " Split." The black tide surged threefold again, like a flowing abyss. " Leave five million to keep gnawing at the tree. The rest—come with me to meet that pig." The zombie boar was still digging up the dirt. The ant army closed in from all directions. At ten meters, it didn't react; only at two meters did it suddenly lift its head. Pitch-black fluid oozed from its wounds. " Snort!" That cry wasn't fear—it was excitement. I hid behind a tree, watching coldly. The zombification had stripped away its wariness but left it even hungrier for fresh flesh. " Go." The boar stamped wildly—hundreds of corpses crushed with each step—and with a single lick of its tongue, thousands more gone. But the black tide was fiercer still, swarming over its entire body in an instant. Sharp mandibles tore off a layer of flesh—yet it didn't retreat an inch, still snorting. No sense of pain. A chill ran through me. No pain, no fatigue, no fear. An enemy like this would only be harder to deal with than a living creature. It devoured the ants, letting its own flesh be gnawed away inch by inch. Bare bones showed, all four limbs severed, and still it kept feeding frantically. " Another million." A fresh black tide poured in, drowning it completely. It struggled for a moment, then its breath cut off. 【Beast Master killed a Level 0 Zombie Boar, gained Experience Points ×5】 【Personal Panel now unlocked】 Experience points... for leveling up? Just as I was about to take a closer look, the bushes in the distance shook violently. A dull, guttural roar. Something big. I grabbed the treasure chest and slipped behind a tree— A brown beast, half a man's height, stepped out from the bushes, a yellow-brown chest set into its back. Another treasure chest—and a bigger one. The giant boar saw the remains on the ground and let out a mournful wail, then stamped in a fury. Hundreds of thousands of ants were reduced to paste in an instant. Emotion—and intelligence. But that chest on its back, I had to have it. " Go." The million-strong black tide turned and lunged, swallowing the beast whole— Yet it emerged unharmed, rolled once on the spot, and crushed hundreds of thousands more. " What's going on?" Little Black sent back a message, just four words: Can't bite through. Hard as stone. 【Notice: Your ants are Level 0 and can only harm Level 0 creatures. Current target is a Level 1 Zombie Boar】 Level suppression. Below Level 1, there was no breaking through its defense. I shook my head and slowly backed away. To get the chest on its back, I'd need another approach. 【Detected 1,200 units of Wood in your possession. Recycle?】 No. The trees for hundreds of meters around had all been gnawed down by Little Black, scattered in heaps across the clearing. Don't recycle. This was my capital for upgrading the cabin, and the surplus could be listed on the market— wood was sure to fetch a sky-high price tonight. The recycle value was only one copper coin per unit, while player trades started at two. Fifty-four until nightfall. minutes. Over a thousand logs—how am I supposed to haul them all back? Everyone else is stressing about chopping down a single tree, while here I am with too much wood. Garbage game. Doesn't even give you a storage system. Storage... Wait. I've got it. The marketplace lets you delist items anytime, and delisted items appear right beside you—no fees, just a limit of nine per batch. List them, then delist—instant teleport home. While hauling, I nudged a log aside and spotted a wood-grain chest by the tree roots. Clean as if it had grown straight out of the soil, completely out of place among the rotting leaves everywhere. I confirmed it was safe and carried it inside. The sky was getting dark. The cabin was packed with wood, and the floor was a swarming mass of little black creatures—I could barely turn around. 【Materials meet upgrade requirements. Upgrade?】 Yes. Fifty logs vanished in an instant. The walls looked brand new, and every broken door and window was fully repaired. Keep going. 【Insufficient materials. Cannot upgrade.】 I froze and opened the panel. 【Building: Small Cabin Level: 1 Defense: 20 Durability: 100/100 (loses 1 point per hour at night; 1 log repairs 1 point) Upgrade Materials: Wood ×200, Stone ×50 Description: Better than 95% of current players. Rating: A barely livable shack】 So it needs stone now. There were plenty of waist-high boulders out in the clearing, but it was getting dark—no time to mine them. I'd have to wait until tomorrow, or see if I could buy some from the marketplace. " Haahh—" I collapsed onto the bed, parched and starving. Eight hours of intense labor had wrung me completely dry. Two treasure chests sat at the foot of the bed. I reached out and touched one, and the info appeared. Too bad my Splitting talent only works on tamed beasts— otherwise I'd split one chest into ten and win without lifting a finger. 【Chest Tiers: Common—Black Iron—Bronze—Silver—Gold—Platinum—Diamond—King—Mythic】 I opened the Common chest first. 【Obtained: Wood ×2, Stone ×1, Bread ×2】 Then the Bronze chest. 【Obtained: Purified Water ×2, Meat ×2, Campfire Blueprint ×1】 The items burst out as fist-sized orbs of light. A touch of my fingertip returned them to their original form, while the chest itself gradually turned transparent and faded away. The bread was palm-sized—enough for a meal. The purified water, five hundred milliliters. The meat, about two pounds. But what really got my heart racing was that yellowed blueprint— 【Campfire Blueprint Materials: Wood ×8 Description: 1 log burns for 2 hours; provides warmth and cooks food】 I built the campfire right away and lit it. Flickering firelight lit up the walls. I set the meat over it, and it started sizzling, dripping grease. I took a bite of the roasted meat and chugged half a bottle of water— Back to life. I opened the regional channel. Zhang Jiwei - Silver Leech: Chopped 6 trees today, 18 logs. Gonna make it through tonight easy! Lin Guorui - ** Golden Otter:** ? Bro, you don't know you can use your beast to chop trees? ** Zhang Jiwei – Silver Leech:** Damn it, why didn't you say so earlier?! Jiang Yiyun – Diamond Mouse:** So jealous of you guys with big beasts. My little mouse gnaws all day and only gets 30 logs. ** Sun Ti – Bronze Python:** We're all short on wood for upgrades. Who's actually gonna sell? ** Zhang Mingtian – Black Iron Wolf:** You guys spend all day just chopping wood? Aren't you starving? I'll trade wood for food and drinks. ** Li Ziba – Golden Cicada:** Selling a Level 1 Hatchet blueprint. Trading for wood, highest bidder wins. DM me your offers. ** Zhao Ritian – Diamond Saber-Tooth:** @Li Ziba Let me see the blueprint. I've got 120 logs today. Nobody in this area can outbid me. ** :** OP, sick! ** :** 120 logs?! So even a human gets scared? I thought you were unstoppable—why run now? Even if you hide inside, that house won't survive a Level 5's relentless assault!" The croc was overjoyed inside— though it didn't dare say a word out loud, wanting only to shrink out of sight and survive until I was dead. " By the way—since you won't talk, then just die." I suddenly turned back, my gaze turning cold as my longsword left its sheath. I had this crocodile figured out: a coward, one who caves to force but never to kindness. Without a little pressure, it would never talk. Dragon-shaped sword energy shot straight at its face. This time, the croc smelled genuine death. This human—he really didn't want the treasure! No. It still wanted to live. That was it—report the location, then stall for time. Just hold out until the Level 5 zombie tore the human to shreds. This human... The user type—falls for this every time. " Wait! The treasure chest is three kilometers that way, on a hill deep in a swamp, next to three big trees!" It spoke fast, desperate to save its own life. " Consider yourself lucky—you just bought yourself another life." I hoisted it up and rushed into the house, sending my army of flying ants racing toward that location. Thud—I flung it into the corner and shut the door. The white tiger zombie shouldn't keep attacking forever... right? That was my guess, but I couldn't be sure. My heart hung in my throat. The giant crocodile sized up the cramped space. So this was a human's shelter—and it had actually reached Level 4. Too bad. Even that couldn't survive three minutes of a Level 5's assault. Thud— A tiger's claw came crashing down, shaking the earth. The cabin lost a bit of durability and swayed violently. Thud—thud— The walls turned transparent, inch by inch. " Heh heh, the moment the human dies, the net breaks, and I burrow straight into the ground." The crocodile counted gleefully—just three more minutes and it'd be free. But a few seconds later, the attacks stopped. A full minute passed. Still nothing. What was going on? Weren't zombies supposed to tear a building apart the instant they laid eyes on it? Wait a little longer—maybe it just got tired. While the crocodile's mind wandered, a line of text popped up before my eyes— 【Congratulations! You are the first to clear the Beast Zombie Horde! Rewards will be distributed after nightfall, along with all other players.】 " Let's go. Take me to that place you mentioned." I let out a breath. That giant tiger zombie had attacked exactly twenty times. No more, no less—strictly bound by the game's rules. My mind raced through the numbers: a Level 2 house lost 75 durability per hit, Level 3 lost 30, and Level 4 only 15. For players stuck with Level 2 houses, this was a death sentence. Countless Level 2 and 3 zombies still roamed outside— and once the durability hit zero, the house could be ripped open with a single swipe. " Go where? Aren't there still Level 5 zombies out there?" The crocodile looked utterly baffled. The memory in its bloodline told it—these zombies wouldn't stop until they'd leveled every building. Yet this human had somehow slipped past them? " Outside. One more word and I kill you." I hurled it out the door. The crocodile hit the ground—no attack came. That tiger zombie really was gone. It was still early, more than an hour until nightfall. I walked into the clearing and started looting corpses. 【Looted Level 0 zombie: obtained Parasitic Vine ×1】 【Looted Level 1 zombie: obtained Parasitic Vine ×2】 " Parasitic vines, all of it?" I was speechless. Looked like the price on these things was about to crash hard. I gathered my spoils and marched the giant crocodile through the forest. " Human, can you put me down? I need to take a dump." Hold it. " Human, the golden treasure chest is actually fa—" The translation: " Yeah." Then you die right now. " No, no, no—I'm telling the truth!" It tried every trick to stop me along the way, but too bad—I wasn't buying it. We soon reached the swamp. Mist swirled everywhere, and a massive mound loomed within the toxic haze. Behind the tall grass, my ant army had already locked onto the cave entrance. " Humans are here—run!" " Croc, didn't you say you wouldn't give away our location?!" " You son of a bitch, you brought a human here!" Swarms of toads and gray wolves burst out of the cave, their eyes filled with terror and hatred. " Little Blacks—kill them." I'd already killed their chieftain. Leaving them alive would only mean trouble later. " Aaah—Croc, may you rot in hell!" " Human, the werewolf investigation envoy arrives in a couple days—spare us!" " Ha, you won't live past tomorrow either!" Screams rose and fell throughout the haze. 【Leafcutter ant killed Level 2 gray wolf. EXP +50】 【Leafcutter ant killed Level 1 toad. EXP +15】 【EXP maxed. Level up?】 Level up! The ant army poured into the cave. Inside were three silver treasure chests—and one more, glowing with golden light. 【Silver treasure chest, upgrading...】 Upgrading? Whatever. Take them all. The mighty tide of ants swept away, carrying the chests. On the clearing, only the Level 4 croc and I remained. " You wiped them all out... Does that mean you can't kill me now?" It sensed a killing intent like never before. " Hand over the treasure you've been using to escape, and I'll give you a chance to fight me. Otherwise, you die in the net." I spread my arms. Power was surging wildly through my body. Level 4. I felt like I'd already surpassed the limits of humanity. I threw a punch, and it whistled through the air. " Fine, I believe you." The croc got serious too. It couldn't break free of the net, and if it refused, all it could do was wait to die in misery. But if I actually let it loose, it might not lose—it was a Level 4 beast, after all. Escaping wouldn't be a problem. Before it even finished speaking, a layer of skin peeled off its body. It was a cloak. " This is called the Earth-Diving Cloak. Wear it, and you can burrow into any soil within twenty meters." It looked heartbroken—this was the crocodile clan's heirloom. " Nice." I'd guessed as much. This croc had a mediocre bloodline, yet it could pull off supernatural feats. Turns out it relied on items. " Grab it!" The net withdrew, and I launched a punch. BAM— The croc flew backward more than a dozen meters. " You—you, you, you... You really made it to Level 4?!" All its fighting spirit collapsed. With a flick of its tail, it fled toward the depths of the swamp. But behind it, a five-meter-long dragon of sword energy roared after it. BAM— The corpse split in two. " Level 4... so strong!" I clenched my fist, spun around, and dashed seven or eight meters in an instant. Time to head back. I'm going to open that— # The Golden Chest I'd never opened a chest this high-level before. Not long after I left, a Level 3 gray wolf came racing back into the mist. " Damn humans—they've wiped out our entire gray wolf clan!" Miasma churned. A two-meter-tall werewolf strode through the fog. Burlap wrapped its lower half, scars crisscrossed its torso, and its wolf's head was twisted in a snarl. " Little Pink, still crying at your age?" " Uncle! You have to avenge the gray wolf clan!" The gray wolf Pink froze for a moment, then broke into delight. " Don't call me Uncle out here. Call me Investigator." The werewolf cleared its throat. "Now— where's the golden chest I left behind?" It wasn't supposed to arrive until the day after tomorrow. It had come two days early just for that chest. " Investigator, sir... the chest was stolen by that human." " Damn it!" The werewolf threw a punch. In an instant, ten-odd meters of swamp evaporated dry. " It's getting late. Tell me—what tricks does this human have?" Know your enemy, know yourself. It wasn't one to act rashly. A long while passed— " You're telling me he killed the Level 4 White Wolf King at Level 3, and now he's leveled up to 4 himself?" The werewolf was stunned. Wasn't it only sent here to deal with one Level 3 White Wolf King? Now there was a Level 4 human who could punch above his weight. " Uncle, can you beat him?" Pink was worried too. This human was growing far too fast. " Call me Investigator." The werewolf snorted coldly. "A mere Level 4 human. I brought a tool from the clan— the Trap-Bell of Golden Confinement. It defends and imprisons at once. Once he's trapped inside, he's dead— unless he can burrow through the earth." " That reminds me. Can he tunnel underground?" Pink thought it over—if he could, the giant crocodile never would've escaped. He answered without hesitation: " I'm certain. He can't." " Good. Tomorrow, we end him." Inside the cabin, the chests were piled into a small mountain. Twenty-one common, twelve black iron, five bronze, two silver. And one silver chest shimmering with a golden sheen. The gold covered even more of the surface than the first one I'd ever seen—the entire chest, nearly eighty percent of it, had turned gold. " Cut down every tree within a four-mile radius just to gather this many." I'd just been through a brutal fight, and my mind was worn thin. Perfect timing to open some chests and unwind. 【Common Chest: Purified Water ×1, Wood ×3】 【Black Iron Chest: Pot Bowl Blueprint ×1, Iron Ore ×1】 【Bronze Chest: Cloth ×1, Fishing Rod Blueprint ×1】 Food, life-skill blueprints, pots and pans and fishing rods—all junk. Not a single thing to boost my combat power. " Mediocre across the board. Now for the silver ones." From silver chests, I'd pulled a *Forest Bestiary* before, and even a precious energy silver coin. 【Silver Chest: Aluminum Alloy ×2, Level 3 Railing Blueprint ×1】 【Silver Chest: Iron Blocks ×3, White 【Silver Ore ×2】 【Silver Ore: Produced from Level 5 ore. A precious material for weapons and armor.】 【Aluminum Alloy: Semi-finished product used to craft weapons and armor. Precious material.】 More materials. The only blueprint was a useless railing—just an upgraded version of the Level 1 fence. " Whether you get good loot always comes down to luck." I felt a little let down. That left only the golden treasure chest still upgrading. 【Golden Treasure Chest Upgrade 92% — Estimated completion in 30 minutes】 " In half an hour... right when the Beast Horde begins." By then, I'd collect the golden chest and the clear reward all at once. " Oh, right—" I still had nearly 200 Parasitic Vines on me. Parasitic Vine was a special material, with no level requirement. It could be used to craft all kinds of armor— a hot commodity, worth about 120 Energy Copper Coins on the market. But its real value wasn't in the price. Before the Beast Horde hit, it was hard currency— enough to trade for rare blueprints and materials that people clutched to their chests and refused to let go of. But once the horde passed, everyone would be swimming in Parasitic Vines—and by then, it'd be worthless. I immediately opened the channel: " Selling special material Parasitic Vine cheap—only trading for precious materials or items of the same tier. Got 6 left, DM me." I didn't mention I had 200. The more you have, the cheaper it gets. The chat exploded instantly— : So many special materials! : How'd this pro get his hands on those? : I'm short on exactly this for my Level 2 armor—DMing now! : Can I trade wood for it? The horde's coming, and having armor makes me feel safer. There were still thirteen thousand players in the zone. With the horde looming, everyone was online, watching and waiting. DMs flooded in— : Boss, trade a Level 2 bow blueprint for 2? Me: No thanks. : 200 wood? Me: Only precious materials or blueprints. : 3 iron blocks for 1, that work? Me: Deal. Plenty of people messaged me, but few had anything I wanted. That's when it hit me— I was way ahead of these players. The treasures in their eyes were nothing special to me. Just as I was about to sell everything off cheap, someone started spamming @ me in the zone channel. Zhao Ritian—Diamond Saber-Tooth: @everyone Nobody trade with Wang Chufeng, or you're making an enemy of the Zhao Alliance! : Young Master Zhao has spoken. We wouldn't dare buy. Sun Ti—Bronze Python: Who the hell do you think the Zhao Alliance is? I'm trading with the boss no matter what. : Whoa, a fight's breaking out! Zhao Ritian—Diamond Saber-Tooth: @Wang Chufeng I told you I wouldn't make life easy for you. Don't even think about selling your stuff! Sun Ti—Bronze Python: @Wang Chufeng My Mutual Aid Alliance will buy your goods at top price. I've had it up to here with Zhao Ritian anyway! One threatening a blacklist, the other jumping out to defy him. For an ordinary person, this... Ke Ding would've thanked Sun Ti, dumped the goods on him cheap, and pissed off Zhao Ritian in the process. Too bad—before Ma Tianqi died, he'd laid out the entire roster of the Zhao Family Alliance. Sun Ti was a core member of the Zhao Family Alliance. He'd signed a contract with Zhao Ritian— zero chance of betrayal. Nice. Putting on a whole song-and-dance routine in front of the entire zone, trying to swindle me out of my Parasitic Vine? Then let's play along. Let's see if you can actually stomach it. I smirked. Just when I was struggling to trade for anything good, someone delivered it right to my door. I posted in the channel: " @SunTi Thanks for the save. But I've got quite a bit of Parasitic Vine, and I only trade it for rare materials and blueprints. Can your Mutual Aid Alliance handle that much?" Sun Ti—Bronze Python: Of course! We're a big group, over fifty members. We can handle it. Sending you a private message now. In the private chat— Sun Ti: Boss, six of yours for a Tier 2 Armor blueprint. Deal? At market rates, the price was fair. But Parasitic Vine was rare—he was still getting the better end. Me: Honestly, I've got over a hundred. Selling them one at a time is a pain. I'd rather move the whole batch. Can you take that many? Sun Ti: Hold on, let me check with the alliance. The moment he exited the chat, Sun Ti's pupils contracted, his breathing quickening. Over a hundred! Had this guy found a way to farm them? This was above his pay grade. He immediately messaged Zhao Ritian. Zhao Ritian: We do need some, but only about twenty. Still, special materials—stockpiling never hurts. Zhao Ritian: Tell him we can't take a hundred-plus. Push the price down as low as it'll go. Trade him those garbage blueprints—the rare ones we can't actually craft. The Zhao Family Alliance had over fifty members. Some lucky ones always rolled treasure blueprints, but without the materials, they couldn't craft them—dead weight, plain and simple. If they could swap those for rare Parasitic Vine? Even if they never used it, they could flip it at a premium later. Guaranteed profit. Sun Ti: No problem! What he didn't know was that once the corpse tide passed, every surviving player would be sitting on dozens, even hundreds of Parasitic Vine. By then—Parasitic Vine would be worthless. The trade list Sun Ti sent over made my pupils shrink. 【Tier 4 Listening Rain Sword Blueprint】【Void Stone】【Copper Ore ×10】... Void Stone, a Tier 4 longsword, copper ore for upgrading buildings—all things I desperately needed. Did Zhao Ritian even know what he was looking at? He was actually willing to hand this stuff over to an enemy. Sun Ti: Boss, 120 Parasitic Vine for any one of these items. One? In your dreams. I opened the Listening Rain Sword blueprint— 【Listening Rain Sword Blueprint · Tier 4】 Crafting Materials: Aluminum Alloy ×2, Molecular Material ×1, Parasitic Vine ×4, Iron Block ×4 Special Ability: Listening Rain. When used in rain or water, combat power increases by 30%! Description: Easily wounds Tier 4 creatures. Aluminum alloy only dropped from Silver Treasure Chests. Molecular material, This was unheard of. No wonder Zhao Ritian was willing to trade—they couldn't make it themselves. But as it happened, I had a piece of aluminum alloy in my hands. The first step in haggling is naming a price the other side can't possibly accept. " You've got twenty items. I pick ten. And don't forget—this parasitic vine is worth over ten thousand copper coins." Sun Ti: Come on, man, our Mutual Aid Alliance has to survive too... Bottom line, five items. Five. I almost laughed out loud. Ten minutes until the Beast Horde. There was no time left to craft armor now—those vines were already worthless to me. " Deal. Since you stood up to Zhao Ritian on my behalf." The items landed in my inventory. I turned my gaze to that chest shimmering with golden light. 【Golden Chest evolution successful!】 【Obtained: Molecular Material ×1, Blueprint of the Thin Illusion ×1】 No titanium alloy. Expected. Opening chests is always a gamble. The molecular material was exactly what I needed— 【Materials for the Listening Rain Sword are complete. Craft now?】 Craft. 【Countdown: 1 hour 24 minutes】 The other blueprint had a strange name. 【Thin Illusion · Gold】 Special Skill: Transformation. Conceal your aura, or mimic another's. Description: Can alter your appearance. Only effective against creatures within two realms above your own. My heart skipped a beat. This was a lifesaver. If I were Level 4 and being hunted by a Level 6—slip this on, blend into the crowd, and I could get away clean. Too bad I'd just used up the molecular material. To craft it, I'd have to wait for next time. The last of the sunset spilled across the clearing as the ant swarm gathered the final batch of timber. " Still a million logs left to collect." I walked toward the woodpile and raised my hand to recall them. Another million energy coins credited to my account. Deep in the forest, other players were locked in combat with the zombie beasts. Some charged in headfirst, some huddled trembling in their cabins, and some screamed frantically for help. Soon enough, people noticed—killing any zombie beast dropped parasitic vines, a hundred times easier than usual. The regional channel exploded instantly. Zhao Ritian stared at his screen, his face twisted with rage. He finally understood he'd been played. " Fine. Fine. Fine." He ground his teeth. "Wang Chufeng, I had no intention of touching you. But since you keep provoking me again and again—four days from now, at the Five Fingers Mountain auction, I'll pour in the full strength of all fifty members of the Zhao Family Alliance, scrape together ten thousand energy coins, and see you dead." The horde receded, leaving devastation in its wake. But the survivors kept their eyes glued to the rankings— who would break into the top ten for clearing the event. 【Distributing Beast Horde Clear Rewards...】 【Congratulations, you cleared it first.】 【Obtained: Evolution Armor · Shallow Sea Heavy Suit】 A suit of silver, brilliantly gleaming heavy armor materialized before me, its weight dropping into my hands like a hundred-pound boulder. 【Shallow Sea Heavy Suit · Platinum · Level 4】 Special Skill Evolution. Every time you level up, this armor levels up with you. Worn on land: Health doubled, speed halved. Worn in water: Breathe and walk underwater freely, no speed penalty, health +30%. Platinum quality. The best piece among all my rewards. Even better—it's finished. No need to slowly gather materials. I can wear it right now. Equip. With the silver armor on, I looked like a legendary general of old. Except every step I took felt alarmingly heavy. " Evolution perk—awesome." Painstakingly crafting armor only to have it become useless after a few days due to leveling up— that's a loss I'll never have to eat again. I glanced at my stats panel. My original 40 health had shot up to 80. Defense 45. In other words, as long as an enemy's hit doesn't exceed 80 damage, I won't die. Life-saving gear, +1. The trade-off—on land, my speed dropped back to level 2. " Can't have it all. Otherwise it would've been way beyond platinum tier." I was satisfied. 【Warning: In seven days, the second Despair Disaster—the World-Ending Rainy Season—arrives! Lasts 15 days. Prepare yourself.】 My pupils shrank. A rainy season, and a world-ending one at that. The entire forest could be submerged in floodwater. And the Shallow Sea Heavy Armor—could breathe underwater, perfectly. So this reward was paving the way for the next disaster all along. But even if I could walk underwater, my wooden cabin couldn't. The disaster was still deadly to me. The regional channel had descended into chaos: — Is this game trying to kill us all?! — They won't just wipe us out, right? There's gotta be a way. — I've tamed fish! This time, it's my turn to save the day! — 666! Before the corpse tide, the region had thirteen thousand people. Now, just over ten thousand remained. Three thousand people, dead in a single night. The Despair Disasters were that terrifying. I closed the channel. Right now, the most important thing was staying alive. The Five-Finger Mountain in four days, the werewolf clan's pursuers, Zhao Ritian's death trap— every one of them demanded real strength. The night was quiet. I fell into a deep sleep. BANG! BANG! BANG— " Zzzt zzzt zzzt... Master, wake up, quick!" Little Black's shrieks cut through my slumber. My eyes snapped open. The cabin was shaking violently, durability—only 34 points left! I'd overslept and nearly gotten raided. I flung out over a hundred logs, patching the durability back to full. Outside the window—it was already daytime. Whatever was attacking me wasn't a creature of the night, but a beast? Through the window, I saw clearly: a level 3 gray wolf, leading a two-meter-tall werewolf, was pounding away at my cabin. Level 5 beasts. Envoys sent by the werewolf clan. It came to tear down my home without a word—so I wouldn't hold back either. I threw on the Earth-Escape Cloak, put on the Shallow Sea Heavy Armor, gripped the Rain-Listening Sword, and shoved the door open— " Dragon Strike!" The five-meter blade of energy took the shape of a massive dragon, hurtling toward the werewolf twenty meters away. " So you're the human who stole my gold treasure chest and killed White Wolf King?" The werewolf smirked, then leapt lightly aside, dodging the blade of energy. Fast! Its speed was far beyond mine. " Little one, I'm talking to you." Before the words even faded, it had closed in beside me, its voice cold and sinister. "It's very rude not to answer." " And tearing down my home—that's polite?" I scoffed, though a chill ran through me. The Shallow Sea Heavy Armor was slowing me down. This fight couldn't be won this way. " Berserk!" My speed surged 50%, matching a Level 4 creature. " Dragon Strike!" A second blade of energy tore through the air. The werewolf didn't dare block it head-on. It dodged aside—from that strike, it caught the scent of death. Bam! I seized the opening, retreated into the house, and slammed the door shut behind me. " Shallow Sea Heavy Armor, off. Deep Blue War Armor, on." If only I had a spatial ring—I could swap gear on the move instead of ducking inside. Lesson learned. I opened the door again. Flowing Cloud Boots, berserk—I burst out as a blur. " Oh? Your speed's almost caught up to mine now," the werewolf narrowed its eyes. "Too bad. I came prepared." " Golden Bell of Binding—go!" A small golden bell flew in from nowhere, dropping over my head and erupting with blinding golden light, trapping me completely. The phantom bell locked me in on all sides. My Rain Listening Sword struck it, but only sparks flew. " A Level 5 binding item." My heart sank. Dragon Strike slammed into it, only making it hum. Right—the Earth Escape Cloak. After so many brutal fights, I'd developed an instinct: this phantom wasn't sealed shut. There had to be a gap underground. I swept the cloak open, and the ground split apart like air. I sank into the earth, my vision reaching thirty meters—as if underwater, I could see everything above. Outside, Little Pink the gray wolf cheered, "Uncle's amazing! Took him down in just a few moves—" " How many times do I have to tell you—out here, call me Investigation Envoy!" the werewolf snarled, its claws lashing out straight for my face. The claw tips were two meters away—a flash of silver flickered over me, and I dove into the earth. The werewolf whipped around, its fierce glare locked on the gray wolf: Didn't you say he couldn't burrow? " It's not my fault, Uncle! That's really what the report said—look out!" I had already burst up from beneath its feet, my Rain Listening Sword wreathed in blade energy, slashing straight for its face. " Enough of your howling!" The werewolf twisted aside, its speed maxing out in an instant. "Human, you're fast— I'll give you that. But you're still one step short of me." I flicked my hand—a white net dropped down over it. A fishing net. It was too fast, so I'd prepared a means to trap it in advance. " A Level 3 net-breaker, and you think you can trap me? Break!" The net shattered— In that instant—my sword arrived. " Dragon's Flight!" The blade's energy tore through its chest, and the sheer force sent it flying more than thirty feet. One move. I'd taken down a Level 5 werewolf in a single move. " Uncle, don't die on me!" "... Call me Envoy." The werewolf was barely clinging to life, yet its gaze swept past its nephew and locked onto me, brimming with venom. "Kill a werewolf, and you'll be branded with the Sirius Mark. Boy, just wait to be hunted down by my kind!" A red glow rose from its body, swirling and twisting as it lunged at me. An unknown technique—I didn't dare take it head-on and darted back into the house. But the red light passed straight through the walls, ignoring them entirely, and sank right into the center of my forehead. **[ You have been branded with the Sirius Mark.]** **[ Any werewolf who sees this mark and kills you will gain all the power of the caster.]** I had nothing to say. Couldn't win, so it slapped a curse on me with its dying breath— weak *and* petty. **[ Killed Level 5 Werewolf. EXP +300.]** Three hundred points. Not bad. I pushed the door open. The gray wolf was hauling the corpse on its back, fleeing for its life. Trying to run? My sword flew from my hand and pinned it to the ground from dozens of yards away. **[ Killed Level 3 Gray Wolf. EXP +100.]** " Little Blacks, get to work." **[ Looted Level 5 Werewolf: Anti-Trap Golden Bell ×1, Qinghe Town Ruins Key ×1.]** Just these two things, and it dared call itself an Investigation Envoy? Pathetic. **[ Qinghe Town Ruins Key: Opens a certain gate within the ruins. Exploration required.]** An ancient iron key, spotted with rust. I couldn't glean anything more from it, so I tucked it away for another day. Right now, the top priority was leveling up. I'd been marked by the Sirius. From here on, every powerful werewolf that crossed my path might come for my life. And that trip to Five Fingers Mountain would be all the more perilous. Without real strength, going there would be suicide. I pulled up my stats panel—and my brow furrowed. **[ Wang Chufeng · Level 4 (715/3000)]** ** Status: Sirius Marked** ** Talent: Infinite Division (SSS Rank)** ** Combat Power: 45** Leveling up to 5 required three thousand EXP. That was the equivalent of—thirty Level 3 beasts. For dozens of miles around, only one place held that kind of reserve. " Zzt zzt zzt—Master! We were chopping trees seven miles out when a swarm of Human-Faced Demon Spiders ambushed us! Heavy casualties!" Little Black's wail jolted me from my thoughts. The spider nest was nine miles away. My tree-chopping hadn't come anywhere near their territory. Couldn't hold back—they'd made the first move? Back when I was Level 3, I'd feared that Level 6 in the nest and hadn't dared provoke it. But now—I'd reached Level 4, with combat power rivaling a Level 5. And I'd gained the Anti-Trap Golden Bell, capable of ensnaring even a Level 6. The strong never wait for the wind to come. Some battles can be avoided for a while, but not forever; rather than wait for someone to break down my door— I'd rather take the initiative and break this stalemate. I smirked, gripping my sword tighter. " All Level 3 grunts, follow me—let's go take on the Human-Faced Demon Spider."

title: Build an Inbound Lead Engine Using Organic Content | Day 44/100 | @DanishWadhwa #digitalagency
transcript:
Getting new clients for agency
through paid ads is great, but what if your client started coming to you
directly through organic content? Hi, I'm Danish Wadhwa, founder
of Webdew , a hundred percent remote digital marketing agency. This is day 44 of a hundred day
series on how to start, build and grow your agency all remote. Let's talk about how to build
an inbound engine using content. One that works 24 by seven. First, speak to a specific
audience on your website at Webdew. When we create content for website
designing or explainer videos, we speak the language of SaaS companies. However, if I'm targeting mortgage
brokers, I make content just for them. This makes your buyer persona
resonate with the copy and make search engine happy. Two, consistent social dominance. One poster a day. Don't aim for a perfect, but just

studies and project stories. It shows we get results and it

match your clients. If your clients lives

mocking laughter filled the room my wife wrapped her arm around her lover and threw $2,000 at me take it and call a taxi home you're disgusting us I walked away called my lawyer and said take back Plaza Hotel each one catching the light from the chandeliers above like fallen leaves in a windstorm around me 200 guests in black tuxedos and evening gowns turned to stare I stood in my brown leather
